A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from PartCraft to PartComposer. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplements are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original part-segmentation experiments, component ablations, generated-image comparisons, automated generation metrics, and a user study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative baseline comparisons, SDXL generations, and additional prompt examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same part-diffusion localization, attention-based mask assignment, localized generation, color guidance, and background preservation procedures. Renaming and implementation on SDXL do not establish a new algorithmic component or procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate segmentation on DeepFashion and CUB200 and part-controlled generation across birds, people, paintings, and cartoon characters. The additional prompts remain within these domains; new baselines and backbones do not introduce a distinct evaluated task or dataset.

E2.justification: v2 Figures 8–9 substantially expand the evaluated comparator set with SD3.5, SD2.1 inpainting with SAM2 masks, PlugNPlay, TurboEdit, ZONE, and MagicBrush. These supplement the retained Stable Diffusion, Rich-Text, and InstructPix2Pix comparisons.

E3.justification: New qualitative protocols include SD3.5 Large prompt generation, inpainting with SAM2 masks and manual part grounding, and PartComposer generation using SDXL. The existing segmentation settings, quantitative generation evaluation, and user-study protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B and Figure 10 add a targeted demonstration of transfer to the SDXL backbone. The component and clustering ablations, attention-map analysis, imperfect-mask robustness examples, and color-leakage failure case already appear in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain the same seed-control statements and user-study reporting: 50 invited participants, 28 complete responses, and approximately 3.5k opinions. Neither adds repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 Figures 8–10 and 12 substantially extend the qualitative findings through new comparator outputs, SDXL generations, and additional prompt examples. Tables 1–2 and Figure 7 retain their numerical results. The reported segmentation advantage changes from at least 10 to at least 5 points in the prose, without changing the underlying scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning for diffusion mixing, localization, mask assignment, and generation are retained. Removing the redundant expanded mixing equation and renumbering or displaying formulas inline do not alter their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: training-free part localization and rich-text-controlled part generation through localized diffusion. The added demonstrations support these existing claims rather than introduce a new core contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds interpretations of newer baselines' localization failures and qualifies quantitative comparability because inpainting requires manual mask grounding. The method's localization bottleneck and color-leakage limitation were already documented in v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds baseline implementation pointers, identifies the SDXL implementation basis, and adds an initial-diffusion blending description. Conversely, v1's explicit generation-localization threshold epsilon = 0.5 and project-page link are omitted. These documentation changes do not establish a changed underlying algorithm.

R1.justification: v2 adds contemporary generation, control, and editing references and distinguishes Ng et al.'s supervised PartCraft from its training-free setting. Section 2 qualifies v1's description of part-level control as unexplored. The separately authored PartCraft is discussed, not experimentally evaluated.

P1.justification: The title and method name change, prose is copyedited, and the supplement gains a contents list and reorganized sections. Attribute examples move to the supplement and limitations move after the conclusion, while the main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, expands the teaser and comparison grids, and adds Figures 8–10 and 12. Existing displays are extensively rearranged, including v1 Figure 6 becoming v2 Figure 13 and v1 Figure 8 becoming v2 Figure 6.

improvement.justification: The newer-baseline comparisons and SDXL demonstration provide useful evidence for localized control and backbone portability. v2 also clarifies its relationship to supervised PartCraft and corrects the overstated segmentation-gain summary. These gains are limited to qualitative additions, while the main quantitative evidence is unchanged; omitted threshold and project-page information slightly weaken reproducibility.
